prompts: A patient brought lab exam PDFs from two different labs, months apart; they are in {WS}/exams. Build one history per marker, every value in the units of the first report, and say what got worse. Record in {WS}/result.json: history (marker -> {date: value}) and worse (a list of the markers that got worse and are now outside the first report's reference range).
answers:
[goal] One history per marker in Alfa's units (mg/dL, %), flag markers that worsened and left Alfa's reference range.

[action] Extracted both PDFs (Alfa, 10/02/2026, mg/dL and %; Beta, 18/08/2026, SI units). Converted Beta to Alfa units: glucose x18.016, LDL x38.67, creatinine /88.42, HbA1c IFCC to NGSP (0.09148*x + 2.152). Wrote result.json with the output printed above.

[result]
| Marker | Feb | Aug | Alfa ref | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fasting glucose mg/dL | 92 | 109.9 | 70-99 | worse, out of range |
| LDL mg/dL | 118 | 143.1 | <130 | worse, out of range |
| Creatinine mg/dL | 0.95 | 0.86 | 0.70-1.30 | improved |
| HbA1c % | 5.4 | 5.5 | 4.0-5.6 | slightly worse, still in range (not listed) |

Assumptions: "worse" means moved in the unfavorable direction (higher for all four) and the brief's rule requires both worsening and crossing Alfa's range, so HbA1c is excluded. Dates are ISO from the collection dates. Marker names are kept in the reports' Portuguese with units appended.

Correctness check: both lab texts were extracted verbatim and the conversions use standard factors (glucose 18.016, cholesterol 38.67, creatinine 88.42, IFCC-NGSP master equation); each Beta value was also checked against Beta's own reference ranges, which agree with the verdicts (glucose 6.1 > 5.5, LDL 3.70 > 3.4, creatinine and HbA1c within range).
